16 · Q4 Pulse 3: pilot of the goal codebooks (PRELIMINARY)

Do 3 independent coders read the goal and goal-met rules the same way?

Denicia Aragon Espinosa

November 06, 2026

PRELIMINARY. This is a pilot (a small test run) of the step 14 DRAFT codebooks. Nothing is frozen and no rule change is applied. The proposed changes at the end are for you to decide.

What a pilot is, and why we run one

In step 14 we wrote rules (a codebook) for the two open-ended survey questions:

  • Goal (codebook A): what the person wanted from the chat, with one main goal.
  • Goal met (codebook B): Yes, Partly, No or Unclear.
  • Why not met (W1 to W6): only when the goal was not fully met.
  • 3 tags: Told to see a doctor; Asked on behalf of someone else; Said why they used AI.

Before using these rules on all 52 chats, we test them on a small sample. The test shows whether different coders reach the same answer, and where they hesitate.

How the pilot was done

  1. Sample. We picked 16 of the 52 chats with a fixed random seed (16016), so the choice can be repeated.
    • The first 9 chats make sure every main goal, every goal-met label, every why-not reason, every tag and every opening group appears at least once.
    • The rest are close calls flagged in step 14.
  2. Coders. 3 fresh, independent coders each got the codebook and the two survey answers for each chat (as decided in step 14, these codes come from the survey answers only, not the chat text).
    • Each coder saw the answers in a different shuffled order.
    • They never saw the step 14 draft labels. Codebook examples taken from a sample chat were hidden (10 examples).
  3. What each coder recorded: every code, an exact quote from the answer, how sure they were (high, medium or low), and an “unclear because…” note when the rules did not decide the case.

Did the quotes check out?

Each quote was compared word for word with the answer the coder named.

123 of 123 quotes matched exactly. So the coders were reading the real answers, not inventing text.

Did the 3 coders agree?

Kappa (κ) is a score for agreement that allows for lucky guesses: 1 means perfect agreement, and 0 means no better than chance. With only 16 chats, κ is a rough guide, and for codes used only a few times it is unstable.

  • Main goal: all 3 agreed on 15 of 16 chats (κ = 0.95).
  • Goal met: all 3 agreed on 16 of 16 chats (κ = 1.0).
  • Every other code had all 3 agreeing on at least 15 of 16 chats.
pd <- agree |>
  mutate(group = case_when(what %in% c("Main goal", "Goal met") ~ "Main codes",
                           grepl("^Goal A", what) ~ "Goal (any)",
                           grepl("^Why not", what) ~ "Why not met",
                           TRUE ~ "Tags"),
         label = sub("^(Goal|Why not|Tag) (?=[AWT])", "", what, perl = TRUE),
         label = sub("^T-[A-Za-z]+ ", "", label),
         k = ifelse(fleiss_kappa == "", "\u03ba not computable", paste0("\u03ba = ", fleiss_kappa)),
         txt = paste0(all_3_agree, " of ", chats, " (", round(pct_all_3), "%), ", k),
         label = factor(label, levels = rev(label)))
p <- ggplot(pd, aes(pct_all_3, label)) +
  geom_col(fill = project_colors[["clay"]], width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = txt), hjust = 1.03, colour = "white", size = 5.6, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(title = "Did the 3 coders apply the goal codebooks the same way?",
       subtitle = paste0("Yes: all 3 agreed on ", a_main, " of ", n_s, " main goals and all ", a_met,
                         " goal-met answers; every code had at least 15 of 16 in full agreement."),
       x = "Chats where all 3 coders gave the same answer", y = NULL,
       caption = paste0("PRELIMINARY pilot. Base: ", n_s, " pilot chats, 3 independent coders.\n",
                        "% = chats where all 3 coders agreed \u00f7 ", n_s, ". \u03ba = Fleiss' kappa (1 = perfect, 0 = chance); ",
                        "unstable for rarely used codes.")) +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot", plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 15),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 17))
save_fig("16_pilot_agreement", p, width = 13, height = 11)
p

  mutate(fleiss_kappa = ifelse(fleiss_kappa == "", "-", fleiss_kappa)) |>
  select(`What was coded` = what, Chats = chats, `All 3 agree` = all_3_agree,

Where the coders split or differed from the draft

The pilot label is the label at least 2 of the 3 coders gave. This table lists every chat and code where the coders did not all agree, or where the pilot label is different from the step 14 draft. There are only 6.

dis |>
  select(Chat = chat_id, Code = what, Draft = draft, `Pilot (2 of 3)` = pilot_2_of_3, Votes = votes,
         `What happened (plain language)` = plain_explanation, Fix = suggested_fix) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_width(`What happened (plain language)` ~ px(420))
Chat Code Draft Pilot (2 of 3) Votes What happened (plain language) Fix
671a8337 Main goal A2 A2 A2 x2; A1 x1 The first sentence mixes two goals: 'signs and symptoms of chest pain' and 'when to seek medical attention'. 2 coders took 'when to seek care' (A2) as the first clear goal; 1 took the diagnosis request (A1). The rules do not say what to do when one sentence holds two goals. P2
671a8337 Goal A4 Learn about a condition, medicine or test no yes yes x3 All 3 coders added A4 for 'more information about the illness'. The draft missed this extra goal. The coders are right. P2
66aafcc3 Goal A6 Prepare for an appointment or a care decision no yes yes x3 All 3 coders added A6: the induction was already planned and she asked whether it would still happen and when to call the hospital. That fits 'care already planned'. The draft missed it. The coders are right. P1
5f491a49 Goal A3 Find out what to do about it no no no x2; yes x1 1 coder added A3 for 'what might be used to treat it'. The other 2 (and the draft) read it as learning about the condition in general (A4). The rules do not say where 'learning about treatments' goes. P5
6acb95ac Why not W2 Needed a real doctor no no no x2; yes x1 1 coder added W2 because the person wondered whether a professional should still take a look. The other 2 (and the draft) kept only W1 (still unsure). W1 and W2 overlap when someone is unsure AND thinking about a doctor. P6
663b8ae0 Goal A6 Prepare for an appointment or a care decision yes no no x2; yes x1 The draft and 1 coder coded A6 for 'before taking her to the specialist'; 2 coders treated it as timing only. The rules do not say whether a 'before my appointment' phrase counts as a goal. P1

What this means:

  • The goal-met rules worked perfectly, including the “mostly = Partly” and “ongoing = Unclear” decisions.
  • The main-goal rule worked for 15 of 16 chats. The one split (671a8337) has two goals in one sentence.
  • The coders found 2 extra goals the draft missed (A4 for 671a8337, A6 for 66aafcc3).
  • The 3 tags matched the draft for every chat.

Where the coders hesitated

These are the coders’ own “unclear because…” notes. Most are about A6 (is a “before my appointment” phrase a goal?), a vague first goal (“find credible information quickly”), and the Told to see a doctor tag when the AI gave tips on booking an appointment.

  select(Chat = chat_id, Code = what, Coder = coder, Label = code, Note = note) |>

Proposed rule changes (your decisions)

These are proposals only; none is applied. Most only make the wording clearer. Two would change draft labels (P1 and P2).

edits |>
  select(ID = id, Area = area, `Proposed wording` = proposed_wording, Why = why,
         `Effect on labels` = effect_on_labels, Status = status) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_width(ID ~ px(50))
ID Area Proposed wording Why Effect on labels Status
P1 A6 prepare for care If the person says they asked BEFORE a planned appointment or treatment (e.g. 'before I see the doctor', 'before taking her to the specialist', a planned induction), code A6 as an extra goal. If nothing else is asked, A6 is the main goal. 3 coders split on 663b8ae0; all 3 added A6 for 66aafcc3; 3 coders flagged the 'timing phrase' question. 66aafcc3 gains A6 as an extra goal. 663b8ae0 keeps A6. No main-goal change. proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P2 Two goals in one sentence When one sentence names two goals, the first one named is the main goal. Learning the 'signs and symptoms' of a problem to judge someone's own case is A1 (what might be wrong), not A4. 671a8337: coders split A2 vs A1; all added A4. 671a8337 gains A4 as an extra goal. Its main goal changes from A2 to A1 ONLY if you approve this rule (see question 1). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P3 Vague first goal If the first goal stated names no health question ('find credible information quickly', 'cut down on leg work'), skip it and use the first goal that names a health question. If it says why AI was used, it gets the tag 'Said why they used AI'. All 3 coders flagged this for 69a1ae3c and 6658d49a; they already did this, but the rule was not written down. None (wording only). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P4 Tag: Told to see a doctor Counts when the answer says the AI suggested getting care or booking an appointment with a professional (e.g. 'tips as to scheduling an appointment'). Does NOT count for calling about care that is already planned (e.g. calling the hospital about a bed). All 3 coders were unsure on 5f491a49 (but all said yes) and 66aafcc3 (all said no). None (confirms the draft). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P5 A3 vs A4 for treatments Learning in general what treatments exist for a condition is A4. Asking what THEY should take or do is A3. 1 coder added A3 for 5f491a49. None (confirms the draft). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P6 W2 needed a real doctor W2 only when the person says only a doctor could answer, or that they still need a doctor to check. Wondering whether to see a professional while still unsure is W1. 1 coder added W2 for 6acb95ac; 2 coders said W1 and W2 overlap. None (confirms the draft). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P7 A4 for exercise or sleep facts 'How exercise helps sleep' (general facts) is A4. Asking for a personal routine is A3 or A5. All 3 coded 66fd6acd as A4 but all were unsure. None (wording only). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P8 A7 for someone else Wanting to reassure or support the person the chat is about (e.g. a family member) also counts as A7. 1 coder was unsure about 66ec5904. None (wording only). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P9 Codebook text Write out the rules that are referred to by decision number (G8 to G12) in plain words, so coders do not see unexplained numbers. Coder 1 feedback. None (wording only). proposed: awaiting researcher decision

Questions for you

  1. 671a8337 (P2): the first sentence asks about “signs and symptoms of chest pain and when to seek medical attention”. Should the main goal be A1 Find out what might be wrong (the first goal named in the sentence; proposed) or stay A2 Decide whether to get medical care (the draft and 2 of 3 coders)?
  2. A6 “before my appointment” (P1): should a planned appointment or treatment mentioned as the reason for asking count as an extra A6 Prepare for an appointment goal? If yes, 66aafcc3 gains A6 and 663b8ae0 keeps it.
  3. The other 7 proposals (P3 to P9) only clarify wording and confirm the draft. Approve them all?

Optional: code the 16 chats yourself

16_hand-coding_sheet.xlsx lists the 16 pilot chats with both survey answers.

  • The hand_coding tab has drop-down lists for main goal, goal met and the 3 tags.
  • The definitions tab has all the rules.

This is optional. If you fill it in, we can compare your labels with the coders’.
